chunks: As though I see you, O Kufah,
you are being drawn out like the tanning of the leather of 'Ukaz, you are being scraped by calamities, and you are being ridden by severe troubles,
and I certainly know that if any tyrant intends evil for you, Allah will afflict him with worry and fling him with a killer!

key_terms.الْعُكَاظِيِّ: of 'Ukaz (a famous market in pre-Islamic Arabia known for its leather goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used to describe the calamities befalling Kufah in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) personifies Kufah as a leather hide being tanned and stretched by the 'Nawazil' (specific calamities) and 'Zalazil' (earthquakes or upheavals), reflecting the city's turbulent political and social history. He assures that any tyrant plotting against the city will be divinely distracted and struck down, a prophecy often linked to the eventual defeat of the Umayyads and Abbasids. This passage highlights the Shia view of Kufah as a testing ground for faith, where divine justice ultimately prevails over earthly oppression.
